subject: Temporary telemetry processor for APAC pilot — DPA amendment needed?
messages:
From: Pete Lin <pete@streamlatch.io>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: rina@fluentops.co
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: New ephemeral telemetry processor for FluentOps pilot

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the sync last week. FluentOps is ready to pilot the APAC edge connector next month; to avoid repeated cold-starts they asked whether we can provision a short-lived telemetry cache operated by StreamLatch for the pilot (expected window: 2026-10-12 -> 2026-11-12).

Quick details:
- Processor: StreamLatch Labs (managed telemetry cache)
- Purpose: short-term KV/prefix cache for debugging and reduced downstream load during pilot
- Data: hashed request IDs, truncated trace spans, non-PII telemetry (no model prompt/response bodies)
- Retention: rolling 7 days by default; can support 0-day retention on request
- Jurisdiction: Singapore (primary), with failover to Tokyo if capacity constrained

We can provide a SOC2 snapshot and a short network diagram; attaching initial pack now.

Question: what documentation do you need from Redwood to process this as a temporary subprocessor (DPA addendum, export-clarity, KMS-crossover)? FluentOps wants to avoid a prolonged legal loop.

If easier, we can do a 20-minute call with security/legal to walk through the artifacts.

Thanks,
Pete
StreamLatch Labs
[pete@streamlatch.io]

---
Attachments: streamlatch-security-pack.pdf, streamlatch-network-diagram.png

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Pete Lin <pete@streamlatch.io>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: New ephemeral telemetry processor for FluentOps pilot

Pete — thanks for the details and the attachments. Looping in Legal (Kimberly), Security (Jordan) and DPA owner (Laura) to confirm what we need to onboard StreamLatch as a temporary processor for the pilot.

Initial asks from my side so we can triage quickly:
- Confirmation that StreamLatch will not receive any prompt/response plaintext or embeddings (you noted non-PII, we need an explicit attestation)
- Proof of encryption in transit and at rest (TLS versions, at-rest encryption details, KMS provider)
- Clarify whether key material crosses jurisdictions (if Redwood KMS ties in)
- Exact retention toggle API and the ability to do on-demand purge for a customer
- Any subcontractors/subprocessors that StreamLatch uses (hosting, CDN, analytics)

If we can get short answers to the bullets above and the SOC2 snapshot is current (past 12 months), Legal can probably draft a one-page DPA amendment + temporary addendum instead of a full DPA revision.

Can the attachments include an exported endpoint list (IP ranges) and a minimal flow diagram that labels data element types (hashed_id, span_meta, etc.)? That will speed Security sign-off.

Proposed next step: 20-minute call tomorrow (Mon 10/5) at 9:30am SGT / 6:30pm PDT — Kim, Jordan, Laura, Pete — can you confirm?

Cheers,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.com

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, Pete Lin <pete@streamlatch.io>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: New ephemeral telemetry processor for FluentOps pilot

Thanks for the context — Mateo.

Legal stance (quick): we can treat StreamLatch as a temporary subprocessor under a DPA amendment provided the following controls are demonstrably in place and documented:
- No access to plaintext model inputs/outputs (written attestation signed by StreamLatch exec)
- Data minimization: list of collected fields and proof of truncation/hashing
- Retention and purge APIs with documented SLAs (we need a documented purge SLA of <= 24 hours upon request from Redwood or the data subject)
- Exportability: clear routing map showing that no data will be routed outside APAC unless failover is triggered — and if failover happens, notice to Redwood + temporary export controls
- Subprocessor chain: list and contact for any third parties used by StreamLatch (hosting, monitoring, backups)
- Insurance and incident contact: attest incident response contact and an IR SLA for notification within 24 hours

Operational note for Security (Jordan): please confirm whether the attached network diagram and the SOC2 snapshot meet our evidence baseline or we need the additional endpoint IP list and cipher-suite details.

If all checks out, Legal will prepare a short addendum (1 page) and an internal temporary approval that expires at pilot end (2026-11-12) unless renewed.

Pete — please confirm you can provide the signed attestation and the purge API docs today so we can target the call and final sign-off tomorrow.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: Pete Lin <pete@streamlatch.io>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, rina@fluentops.co
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: New ephemeral telemetry processor for FluentOps pilot

Kim, Mateo — thanks. Attaching the signed attestation and a short purge API spec (two small files) — shipping both as PDFs. Answers inline below: 

- Plaintext access: confirmed. StreamLatch will never ingest model prompts or model outputs. We operate on hashed request ids + telemetry metadata only. Signed attestation attached (signed by our Head of Ops).
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ for transit, AES-256 at rest. We use AWS KMS (customer keys are supported but not required for this pilot). No Redwood KMS integration for the pilot; keys are managed by StreamLatch in SG KMS.
- Retention/purge: rolling 7-day window. Purge API supports immediate purge per-tenant; we guarantee purge propagation within 12 hours across replicas. Purge doc attached (purge-api-spec.pdf).
- Subprocessors: hosting on AWS Singapore (no additional third-party analytics vendors). We do use CloudMetrics for platform telemetry (we have that listed in the attestation) but CloudMetrics does not receive customer telemetry data — only StreamLatch platform health metrics.
- Failover: if Singapore capacity is exceeded we may route to our Tokyo cluster; we will provide 48h notice and request emergency export approval from Redwood if that occurs.

Call: the 9:30am SGT / 6:30pm PDT slot works for our team — we’ll be on standby.

Best,
Pete Lin
Head of Partnerships | StreamLatch Labs
pete@streamlatch.io

---
Attachments: streamlatch-attestation-signed.pdf, purge-api-spec.pdf
